t:
For the development, modernization, and enhancement of, modifications to, and infrastructure for Department-wide and program-specific information technology systems, for the continuing operation and maintenance of both Department-wide and program-specific information systems, and for program-related maintenance activities, $280,000,000, of which $260,000,000 shall remain available until September 30, 2021, and of which $20,000,000 shall remain available until September 30, 2022:  Provided, That any amounts transferred to this Fund under this Act shall remain available until expended:  Provided further, That any amounts transferred to this Fund from amounts appropriated by previously enacted appropriations Acts may be used for the purposes specified under this Fund, in addition to any other information technology purposes for which such amounts were appropriated:  Provided further, That not more than 10 percent of the funds made available under this heading for development, modernization and enhancement may be obligated until the Secretary submits to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations, for approval, a plan 
for expenditure that—(A) identifies for each modernization project: (i) the functional and performance capabilities to be delivered and the mission benefits to be realized, (ii) the estimated life-cycle cost, and (iii) key milestones to be met; and (B) demonstrates that each modernization project is: (i) compliant with the Department’s enterprise architecture, (ii) being managed in accordance with applicable life-cycle management policies and guidance, (iii) subject to the Department’s capital planning and investment control requirements, and (iv) supported by an adequately staffed project office.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that requiring a plan to be submitted "for approval" before funds are obligated is a participatory check on a federal decision. But the approving bodies are the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations, which are inside the federal government. The rest of the section is an appropriation for information technology systems, with no role for states, the public, outside experts, or any other non-federal party.
fable.s: may be obligated until the Secretary submits to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations, for approval, a plan

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary to submit a plan to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations. Congress and its committees are part of the federal government. Therefore, this interaction is internal to the government and does not involve participation by outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities.
qwen_block.s: not more than 10 percent of the funds made available under this heading for development, modernization and enhancement may be obligated until the Secretary submits to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations, for approval, a plan

opus.w: The only process step here is that the Secretary must submit an expenditure plan to the House and Senate Appropriations Committees for approval. Those committees are part of Congress, so this approval stays inside the federal government. The approval requirement may look like outside sign-off on a federal decision, but no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted. The rest of the section just appropriates funds and says how long they remain available.
opus.s:
not more than 10 percent of the funds made available under this heading for development, modernization and enhancement may be obligated until the Secretary submits to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations, for approval, a plan

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to submit a plan to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations for approval. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this interaction is intra-governmental and does not constitute participation with parties outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: not more than 10 percent of the funds made available under this heading for development, modernization and enhancement may be obligated until the Secretary submits to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations, for approval, a plan
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that submitting a plan to Congress involves "participation" because it requires interaction with an external body. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to or seeking approval from congressional committees is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
